claim: NASA JPL processes about 4.4 TB of downlinked satellite data a day into up to 70 TB of data products on automatic scaling fleets: Spot Instances for the fault-tolerant processing and On-Demand with Capacity Reservations for critical processing.

automatic scaling fleets that react to the dynamic workload demands

claim: Since November 20, 2025, an instance refresh can use the ReplaceRootVolume strategy: it replaces only the root EBS volume while the instance keeps running, so no new instance is launched and network interfaces, IP addresses, non-root volumes, security groups and IAM roles are preserved.
question: What does root volume replacement during an instance refresh do, and when was it added?

values.display: replacing only the root EBS volume while keeping the instance running
November 20, 2025

evidence.quote: Root volume replacement updates your instances by replacing only the root EBS volume while keeping the instance running.
This removes the need to launch new instances and avoids potential capacity constraints.
The original root volume is detached, a new root volume is created from your specified AMI, and then attached to the same instance.

| [Replace root volumes](#DocumentHistory) | Root volume replacement updates your instances by replacing only the root EBS volume while keeping the instance running. For more information, see [ Replace root volumes during instance refresh](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/replace-root-volume). | November 20, 2025 |

claim: Replace Root Volume cannot be used when the group or the desired configuration uses the $Latest or $Default launch template version, or when the group has a warm pool; if the replacement fails on an instance, the instance is terminated and replaced.

values.display: uses the `$Latest` or `$Default` launch template version
has a warm pool
marks that instance for termination and replaces it with a new instance

qualifiers.scope: per instance refresh with the ReplaceRootVolume strategy

evidence.quote: You can’t start an instance refresh with Replace Root Volume if the EC2 Auto Scaling group or the instance refresh desired configuration uses the `$Latest` or `$Default` launch template version.

If root volume replacement fails for an instance, Auto Scaling marks that instance for termination and replaces it with a new instance.

continues to maintain its desired capacity even if an instance becomes unhealthy

claim: Choose scheduled scaling when you know exactly when capacity must change because demand follows a predictable schedule; choose dynamic scaling when traffic changes at times you cannot predict.

when you don't know when the traffic will change

evidence.quote: This is useful when you know exactly when to increase or decrease the number of instances in your group, simply because the need arises on a predictable schedule.

claim: A group can use several policy types together: dynamic scaling policies can be combined, and predictive scaling (proactive) can be combined with dynamic scaling (reactive) to add instances ahead of daily and weekly patterns.

claim: Target tracking assumes the metric is inversely proportional to group capacity (when capacity grows the metric should fall by about the same proportion), so a total such as pending jobs must be converted to a per-instance average with metric math.

values.display: inversely proportional to the capacity of the Auto Scaling group
convert existing metrics into average per-instance

evidence.quote: Converting metrics is essential because target tracking assumes that the metric is inversely proportional to the capacity of the Auto Scaling group.
So when capacity increases, the metric should decrease by nearly the same proportion.
Metric math is particularly useful to convert existing metrics into average per-instance.

claim: Well-Architected defines immutable infrastructure as a model where no updates, security patches or configuration changes happen in place; a change is built onto new infrastructure and deployed, which also lets remote access such as SSH be disabled.
question: What is immutable infrastructure, and what security benefit does it bring?

values.display: no updates, security patches, or configuration changes happen in-place on production workloads
remote access mechanisms (such as SSH) can be disabled

evidence.quote: Immutable infrastructure is a model that mandates that no updates, security patches, or configuration changes happen in-place on production workloads.
When a change is needed, the architecture is built onto new infrastructure and deployed into production.
By not allowing changes to infrastructure, remote access mechanisms (such as SSH) can be disabled.

claim: With immutable deployments the previous working version is not changed, so you can roll back to it when errors are detected; deployments either complete or change nothing.
question: Why are immutable deployments safer to roll back?

values.display: the previous working version is not changed

evidence.quote: Deployments are safer because the previous working version is not changed.
You can roll back to it if errors are detected.
Deployments either complete successfully or nothing changes, increasing consistency and reliability in the deployment process.

claim: The TerminateInstanceInAutoScalingGroup API now accepts up to 100 instance IDs in one call (batch termination); lifecycle hooks and load balancer connection draining still apply to each instance, at no additional cost.
question: How many instances can one TerminateInstanceInAutoScalingGroup call terminate?

values.display: up to 100 instance IDs
no additional cost

evidence.quote: You can now pass up to 100 instance IDs to the TerminateInstanceInAutoScalingGroup API to terminate them as a batch, reducing the number of API calls needed to scale down your Auto Scaling groups.

All instances in a batch are validated atomically before termination begins, and existing Auto Scaling behaviors such as lifecycle hooks and load balancer connection draining are preserved for each instance in the batch.
This feature is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost.
